Edgerunners renewed interest in Cyberpunk 2077, helped turn around the game's negative perception after its rocky launch, and is held as one of the greatest video game adaptations of all time. So it’s no exaggeration to say that Edgerunners is an incredibly hard act to follow. items.t: Oakland Police Officers Association building targeted by cash-seeking burglar
items.x: (KRON) The Oakland Police Officers Association said its building was targeted by a burglar, according to a spokesperson. The OPOA building is located at 555 5th St. in Oakland. The OPOA said the male suspect was searching for cash and eventually stole money from an office cabinet. "No files of information were impacted by the break-in and theft. The suspect was captured by police nearby while attempting another burglary, the OPOA said. "This demonstrates, sadly, that no one, not even police officers, is immune to ongoing crime in Oakland," added OPOA spokesperson Sam Singer.

items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: What is the ‘Couch Economy’ costing you?
items.x: ( NerdWallet ) I get groceries delivered about three times a month. From my couch, I can also order dinner, buy a dress for an upcoming wedding and stream a movie. Many months, a solid chunk of my budget gets spent without me even leaving the house. This is the new “couch economy,” according to a recent report from Visa . In the couch economy era, more and more domestic spending is happening online — 58% in 2026 in the U.S., compared to 48% in 2019, based on Visa transactions. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. All of these things that are downstream — for example, your immune system, your energy — don’t match up quite as well,” said

items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. All of these things that are downstream — for example, your immune system, your energy — don’t match up quite as well,” said

items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. According to Schefter, multiple teams have reached out to the Colts and talks are active and ongoing. Among the teams that have reportedly reached out, the Denver Broncos, Green Bay Packers, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants, and Seattle Seahawks were interested in Taylor, Schefter's sources said. It was also reported that Taylor and Colts owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon had an in-depth conversation about the future of the team earlier this week. Taylor, 27, is a three-time Pro Bowler and has been with the Colts since 2020. He is currently under contract through the 2027 season. This news comes after the Colts traded away franchise players Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, along with firing longtime GM Chris Ballard earlier in the week.

items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Judge blocks DOJ from threatening election officials over noncitizen voting claims
items.x: ( The Hill ) A California federal judge Friday ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening election officials with criminal prosecution in its ongoing efforts to crack down on noncitizen voting. items.t: IMPD: Child dead after drowning on Indy’s west side
items.x: INDIANAPOLIS — A child is dead after drowning in a retention pond on the city's west side on Friday evening. The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department confirmed to FOX59/CBS4 that officers were called to the 600 block of Magdalene Lane around 6:30 p.m. on reports that a young child was seen entering the water and had not been seen coming back up. The scene of a suspected child drowning on the west side of Indianapolis, captured by a FOX59/CBS4 crew. A fire and rescue team was reportedly called to the scene, where they retrieved a child from the water and immediately transported them to Riley Hospital for Children. The child was pronounced dead at the hospital. No additional information has been provided at the time of this article's publication. This is a developing story; check back for updates.

items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Healthcare becomes key midterm issue ahead of policy changes

Policy analysts warn the loss of coverage will impact hospital systems. items.t: Appeals court rules against Trump — again — on California ballots
items.x: ( The Hill ) A split federal appeals court panel again rejected the Trump administration's bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots it says are likely noncitizens until they can be verified. The 2-1 majority on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit didn’t dispute a lower court’s finding that the list isn’t credible and ruled the administration’s position would undermine the Constitution. “As the district court found—and we discern no clear error—there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system,” the majority wrote in its unsigned opinion. The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: What’s At Stake For Black Americans In The 2026 Midterms
items.x: The 2026 midterm elections will determine which party controls the House of Representatives and Senate, shaping what legislation Congress advances, which policies receive funding and how the federal government oversees existing programs. The party in control of each chamber has significant influence over whether bills addressing health care, voting rights, education, housing and workers' rights move forward or stall. Those decisions can have direct consequences, from access to affordable medical care to the ability of Black communities to elect representatives of their choice. items.x: Nationwide Tia Tate made history in 2023 when she became the first Black woman hired as a firefighter by the Killeen Fire Department in Texas. A Killeen native, she now serves the community where she grew up. Her path to the profession began after a traumatic experience made her realize she wanted the skills to help people during emergencies. The Killeen Fire Department, established in 1920, had never hired a Black female firefighter before Tate joined its ranks. A 2012 graduate of Killeen High School, she said returning to serve her hometown made the achievement especially meaningful. However, she did not initially realize she was breaking a barrier. Her mother, Peandra Hinton, said she did not know her daughter had been taken to the pumpkin patch. She also said the toddler was with a group of people she did not know. items.x: Nationwide Jeorgi Golden, an African American woman from Richmond, Virginia, who spent 35 years working as a hairstylist and nail tech, is now battling lung cancer after decades of exposure to salon chemicals. She says beauty professionals received little information about the potential dangers of these chemicals during her career. Golden entered the beauty industry in the late 1970s or early 1980s. Over the years, she built close relationships with clients who often treated their salon visits as an opportunity to share personal struggles. items.t: First Black Student at Mississippi State University Sadly Passes Away at 82
items.x: Nationwide Dr. Richard E. Holmes, who was the first African American student at Mississippi State University, has died at 82. The Starkville native made history by breaking a racial barrier at the university in 1965. He later built a career in medicine before returning to the university to care for its students. Holmes enrolled at Mississippi State on July 19, 1965, becoming the first Black student in the university’s history. His arrival came during a period when racial segregation and resistance to integration remained widespread across Mississippi. He continued his studies at the university, earning a liberal arts degree in 1969 and a master’s degree in microbiology in 1973, according to WLBT . items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. All of these things that are downstream — for example, your immune system, your energy — don’t match up quite as well,” said

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." All eyes are on Mississippi's midterm election, where Scott Colom s fighting chance to upset Republicans could see him flip a U.S. Senate seat that hasn't been won by a Democrat in a generation since 1982 to be exact. Just days away from Nov. 3, Colom is closing in on Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith . Polls show him trailing the Republican by just 5 points in a red state that elected Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election by 23 points. The race is so competitive that it has attracted big-name Democrats, including former U.S. Presidents Barack Obama and Bill Clinton and former U.S. Vice President Kamala Harris . items.t: Javits Was Supposed to Be Here
items.x: Eight years after Junior, the Bronx is burying another 15-year-old. "Crime is down" is not an answer. I walked the same Bronx streets that Javits Frimpong walked. Throughout my teenage years, I understood that my life could be in danger at any moment, or that my freedom could be threatened by a choice I might be forced to make. When you grow up surrounded by that reality and survive it, something dangerous can happen: You begin to normalize it. You convince yourself it wasn't that bad, that things will eventually get better. That is the lie I want our young Black men to unlearn. The sickness that has eaten at our communities is not who we are. We are worth something. Life is worth living. And there is more out there than what this country has conditioned us to believe, more than the brutal environment too many of our neighborhoods are left to endure. items.t: Cerina Fairfax's sister calls for divorce law reform six months after former Virginia lieutenant governor killed her
items.x: Arisce Wanzer recalls her sister's final months and questions Virginia's one-year separation requirement. Six months after Dr. Cerina Fairfax was killed by her estranged husband , former Virginia Lt. Gov. Justin Fairfax, her family is still struggling to make sense of the tragedy. Now, her sister is calling for changes to Virginia's divorce laws , hoping other families can avoid similar heartbreak. In an emotional interview with NBC Washington , Arisce Wanzer remembered her sister as a devoted mother, successful dentist and the person everyone in their family could count on. “We could have never imagined it would end like this,” Wanzer said, speaking from her home in Australia. On April 16, police say Justin Fairfax, 47, fatally shot his wife, 49, inside their Annandale, Virginia, home before taking his own life. Their two teenage children were home at the time, and their son called 911.

items.t: Southern California doctor sentenced to prison for $45 million Medicare fraud scheme
items.x: ( KTLA ) A Southern California doctor was sentenced to 15 years in prison for defrauding Medicare out of more than $45 million and using the money to fund a luxury lifestyle. Violetta Mailyan, 45, of Glendale, owned and operated Healthy Way Medical Center, a clinic that claimed to provide beauty and cosmetic services, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. “Although Medicare reimburses medical providers for Botox injections when necessary to treat documented cases of chronic migraines, Mailyan billed and received payments for thousands of injections that were never provided,” prosecutors said. Many of the billed injections were either provided for cosmetic purposes only or were given to patients whose primary care physicians had not referred them for treatment of chronic migraines. items.t: Sheriff Chip Hughes shares advice for a safe Halloween
items.x: CRAVEN COUNTY, N.C. (WNCT) Craven County Sheriff Chip Hughes is ensuring that everyone has a safe and exciting Halloween by sharing some safety tips. Motorists: • Watch for children darting out from between parked cars. • Watch for children walking on roadways, medians and curbs. • Enter and exit driveways and alleys carefully. • At twilight and later in the evening, watch for children in dark clothing. Parents: • Make sure that an adult or an older responsible youth will be supervising the outing for children under age 12. • Check the sex offender registry when planning your child’s trick-or-treat route. You can view maps that pinpoint registered offenders’ addresses in your neighborhood and sign up to get email alerts when an offender moves nearby. • Plan and discuss the route trick-or-treaters intend to follow. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: What is the ‘Couch Economy’ costing you?
items.x: ( NerdWallet ) I get groceries delivered about three times a month. From my couch, I can also order dinner, buy a dress for an upcoming wedding and stream a movie. Many months, a solid chunk of my budget gets spent without me even leaving the house. This is the new “couch economy,” according to a recent report from Visa . In the couch economy era, more and more domestic spending is happening online — 58% in 2026 in the U.S., compared to 48% in 2019, based on Visa transactions. About a quarter of active U.S. Visa cards are used for 10 or more online or in-app transactions per month, a near-doubling since 2019. “What we can see is a meaningful shift in how and where consumers transact,” said Mohamed Bardastani, principal CEMEA economist at Visa, in an email. “The strongest evidence is the rise in frequent online and in-app purchasing.” Visa’s research doesn’t show whether people are spendi

items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.x: ( The Hill ) A California federal judge Friday ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening election officials with criminal prosecution in its ongoing efforts to crack down on noncitizen voting. U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson issued a temporary restraining order connected to a lawsuit brought by unions representing California election workers earlier Friday. items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Appeals court rules against Trump — again — on California ballots
items.x: ( The Hill ) A split federal appeals court panel again rejected the Trump administration's bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots it says are likely noncitizens until they can be verified. The 2-1 majority on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit didn’t dispute a lower court’s finding that the list isn’t credible and ruled the administration’s position would undermine the Constitution. “As the district court found—and we discern no clear error—there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system,” the majority wrote in its unsigned opinion. The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: What is the ‘Couch Economy’ costing you?
items.x: ( NerdWallet ) I get groceries delivered about three times a month. From my couch, I can also order dinner, buy a dress for an upcoming wedding and stream a movie. Many months, a solid chunk of my budget gets spent without me even leaving the house. This is the new “couch economy,” according to a recent report from Visa . In the couch economy era, more and more domestic spending is happening online — 58% in 2026 in the U.S., compared to 48% in 2019, based on Visa transactions. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: ( The Hill ) A California federal judge Friday ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening election officials with criminal prosecution in its ongoing efforts to crack down on noncitizen voting. U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson issued a temporary restraining order connected to a lawsuit brought by unions representing California election workers earlier Friday. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating

In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: 29,000 gallons of sewage spills in Long Beach; many swimming areas closed
items.x: A large sewage spill has led to the closure of many swimming areas in Long Beach, officials announced Saturday. The City of Long Beach stated in a press release that an estimated 29,000 gallons of sewage discharged near Livingston Drive and 2 nd Street starting at 6:30 p.m. Friday. “The spill was associated with a force main break on a pressurized pipe that conveys wastewater,” city officials said, citing a report from the Long Beach Utilities Department. Flow has since been rerouted, and contractors for the city have been deployed to help with spill cleanup. Of the 29,000 gallons that spilled, 15,000 was recovered while 14,000 discharged into the ocean. Long Beach City Health Officer Dr. Cliff Okada ordered the temporary closure of all open coastal swimming areas, bay swimming areas and lagoons as recreational water quality is affected. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. items.t: McDonald’s McRib lawsuit moves forward over claims sandwich contains no rib meat: reports
items.x: McDonald's must face a lawsuit accusing the fast-food giant of misleading customers about what is actually inside its popular McRib sandwich, a federal judge ruled Friday, according to multiple reports. The proposed class action lawsuit alleges that despite its name and distinctive rib-like shape, the McRib contains no actual pork rib meat, leading customers to believe they are purchasing a more expensive cut of pork, the Economic Times reports. U.S. District Judge April Perry in Chicago rejected McDonald's attempt to dismiss the lawsuit in its entirety, allowing consumer deception, fraud and unjust enrichment claims to proceed, according to FOX Business. Five other claims were dismissed without prejudice. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: Former police sergeant charged with sexually assaulting 2 women who worked for the department
items.x: A former Garden Grove police sergeant was charged with sexually assaulting two women who worked for the department. The Orange County District Attorney’s Office identified the suspect as Charles “Chuck” William Starnes III, 52. Starnes is accused of sexually assaulting two women in two separate incidents. A March 2007 incident involved a female officer at a Stanton bar, court documents said. As she left the restroom, Starnes is accused of sexually assaulting her. He allegedly dragged the woman out of the bar and into the parking lot, where he continued assaulting her until he was stopped by two other officers. In March 2020, he was accused of sexually assaulting a female civilian police employee. The alleged assault happened during a car ride after the victim and Starnes left a party in Long Beach to celebrate the completion of their police officer probationary period, prosecutors said.

items.x: While a few light showers or areas of drizzle remain possible from time-to-time through Sunday afternoon, that rain will not amount to much. Accumulated rainfall will likely remain under a tenth of an inch for most who see additional rainfall between Saturday night and Sunday. A more widespread and soaking rain will approach the region with our next weather system beginning Monday. items.t: Forreston gets revenge on Lena-Winslow in Round One matchup
items.x: FORRESTON, Ill. (WTVO/WQRF) — Forreston lost to Lena-Winslow in week 3 of the regular season. Now it was a different ball game in round one of the Playoffs. Forreston was the first team to score; Connor Politsch hit Eli Ferris in the middle of the field for a Passing touchdown. Lena-Winslow would answer back with a multi-play drive ending in a Merrik Mahon 2-yard rushing touchdown. Forreston drove right down the field as well and had a touchdown of their own with a Connor Politsch rushing touchdown. The game would be 16 to 6 at the half. In the second half, it would be primarily defense, as neither team would be able to find the end zone until the final moments of the game. Politsch handed it off to Jonathan Milnes as he put the icing on the cake. Forreston defeated Lena-Winslow 22 to 6. Forreston will face Stockton next week in round 2. items.t: Winnebago County K9 Quatro dies after sudden medical condition
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — The Winnebago County Sheriff's Office announced Saturday that K9 Quatro has died following what officials described as a sudden medical condition. In a post on X, the sheriff's office said, "It is with heavy hearts that we announce the passing of WCSO K9 Quatro, after a sudden medical condition." No additional details were immediately available. A law enforcement procession was scheduled to depart at 8:10 p.m. from the Animal Emergency Clinic of Rockford on Spring Creek Road and travel to the Winnebago County Coroner's Office. Quatro joined the Winnebago County Sheriff's Office in September 2021. In a June 2025 Facebook post , the sheriff's office described Quatro as "always giving 110%" while serving Winnebago County. This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

items.t: Applications open for energy assistance programs
items.x: As colder weather approaches, energy assistance is available to help offset winter heating costs. The federal Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) provides funding to assist eligible households with home energy expenses. Illinois LIHEAP You must be a resident of Illinois and a U.S. citizen or legally admitted for permanent residence. You must live in the household and be responsible for paying the home energy/utility bill (or rent that includes utilities). Your household’s combined gross income for the 30 days prior to application must be at or below 300% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines or 60% of the State Median Income (SMI). To apply, Illinois residents in Rock Island, Mercer and Henry counties can contact Project NOW at 309-793-6391. Residents can also call the Illinois LIHEAP hotline at 833-711-0374. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: Why St. Louis trick-or-treaters tell jokes for candy on Halloween
items.x: ST. LOUIS – Thousands of trick-or-treaters will go door-to-door Saturday across the St. Louis region, dressed in costumes and ready to fill their bags with candy. But some may need to earn their tasty treats with a sense of humor. As part of a Halloween tradition, at least for some St. Louis-area households, your child might be asked to tell a joke in exchange for candy. This may come as a surprise to parents who venture out with their children for the first time, families who recently moved to the St. Louis area, or are out-of-towners. It’s hard to pinpoint exactly when this started, but jokes have been part of the St. Louis trick-or-treating experience for decades. But why? That depends on who you ask. items.t: A mild Halloween forecast with light rain or sprinkles possible at times
items.x: ST. LOUIS We have a mild and mostly dry Halloween ahead, with only a few intermittent sprinkles or areas of light rain possible. Temperatures will be in the low 70s with mostly cloudy to overcast skies. For trick-or-treaters, we can expect a few sprinkles or showers, especially by late evening, but certainly not a wash out. Scattered showers are possible tonight and Sunday morning. Sunday will be cooler with highs only in the mid 60s and cloudy skies. A stronger storm system arrives late Monday, bringing the potential for widespread, beneficial rainfall that could continue through Wednesday.

items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: ST. LOUIS COUNTY, Mo. Early voting in St. Louis County has officially surpassed the total early voting turnout from the entire 2022 midterm election. More than 130,000 voters in St. Louis County have already cast their ballots ahead of Tuesday's Election Day, Nov. 3. St. Louis County elections official Eric Fey reported that early participation has more than doubled compared to the previous midterm cycle. “In 2022 we have a little over 56,000 people vote early. We have had over 130,000 people vote this election,” he said. Republican Director of Elections Rick Stream stated that election authorities are predicting overall voter turnout between 55% and 60%.
