items.t: Mid America Adventure clears out St. Louis merch, retires Fright Fest name after 2026 season
items.x: EUREKA, Mo. This weekend marks Fright Fest at the theme park formally known as Six Flags St. Louis, now operating as Mid America Adventure. It also marks the park's final weekend of operation for the 2026 season. With new owners and a new name, it's the last time parkgoers will have a chance to purchase theme park merchandise with "St. Louis" in the name. When Enchanted Parks bought Six Flags St. Louis and six other parks, they began a name change and rebranding. The 342-million-dollar acquisition means familiar Warner Brothers characters and coaster names inside the park are going away. But not the rides. They’ll be renamed. The renamed Mid America Adventure is holding the longtime annual Fright Fest celebration, which will also be renamed after this year. items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." The shop opened just last year and is already having to rethink what it can sell. He says some imported wines now cost 10% more – with those higher costs passed on to customers. M

items.t: Southern California doctor sentenced to prison for $45 million Medicare fraud scheme
items.x: ( KTLA ) A Southern California doctor was sentenced to 15 years in prison for defrauding Medicare out of more than $45 million and using the money to fund a luxury lifestyle. Violetta Mailyan, 45, of Glendale, owned and operated Healthy Way Medical Center, a clinic that claimed to provide beauty and cosmetic services, according to the U.S. Department of Justice. “Although Medicare reimburses medical providers for Botox injections when necessary to treat documented cases of chronic migraines, Mailyan billed and received payments for thousands of injections that were never provided,” prosecutors said. Many of the billed injections were either provided for cosmetic purposes only or were given to patients whose primary care physicians had not referred them for treatment of chronic migraines. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: NORTH LITCHFIELD BEACH, S.C. (WBTW) — A dead humpback whale washed ashore near Pawleys Island, prompting wildlife experts to perform a necropsy to determine how the animal died. Officials with the Lowcountry Marine Mammal Network believe the whale had been dead for approximately a week before washing ashore. The organization is urging the public to avoid approaching or touching the carcass because marine mammals can carry diseases. Researchers are examining the whale for signs of physical trauma, although its advanced state of decomposition could make determining a cause of death difficult. “At this point in the state of decomposition, the main thing we’re going to be looking for are any broken bones to see if the animal maybe was hit by a ship or boat,” said Lauren Rust, executive director of the Lowcountry Marine Mammal Network. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. The Conway Police Department said officers responded to the crash at about 12:04 p.m. Saturday at the Chili’s restaurant in Conway. Preliminary information indicates the driver accidentally drove into the building, police said. The Conway Chili’s had recently undergone renovations, according to police.

items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title

items.x: (NewsNation) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides, according to a new coroner's report. Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: What is the ‘Couch Economy’ costing you?
items.x: ( NerdWallet ) I get groceries delivered about three times a month. From my couch, I can also order dinner, buy a dress for an upcoming wedding and stream a movie. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: AAA advises drivers about daylight saving time
items.x: ( WAVY ) – Overnight, we trade one extra hour of sleep for months of darkness as we leave work to drive home. And even though we're on the easier end of the time transition (from daylight saving time to standard time), the switch still takes its toll. Nexstar's WAVY went to AAA Tidewater Virginia to see what commuters can expect. "Well, the biggest thing for drivers will be the change in daylight when we leave work or school," said Holly Dalby with AAA. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Detectives met with Florida lab scientists for help advancing Nancy Guthrie investigation: deputies
items.x: TAMPA, Fla. (WFLA) — Arizona detectives investigating the disappearance of Nancy Guthrie, the 84-year-old mother of “Today” show host Savannah Guthrie, recently traveled to Florida for help in the case. According to the Pima County Sheriff's Office, investigators met with lab scientists in Florida earlier this month to see what more could be done to advance the case. Detectives are reportedly hoping to further their DNA analysis in the investigation. "A number of ideas were discussed, and we continue to work with all of our partners to solve this case," deputies wrote in a statement posted to social media on Friday. Deputies ask anyone with information to call 88-CRIME or 1-800-CALL-FBI. "We want to remind the public that no tip is too small," deputies said. "Even the smallest piece of information could be critical to the investigation."

items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

The Lisa Leslie Award, now in its 10th year, recognizes the top center in NCAA Division I women’s college basketball. It is named after the three-time All-American, 1994 National Player of the Year, and Class of 2015 Hall of Famer. Ngodu transferred to the Mountaineers from UCF this offseason, where she spent the first three years of her college career. Last season, she set career-highs with 10.8 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.3 blocks per game. Despite missing several games due to injury, she finished top-10 in the Big 12 in total rebounds, defensive rebounds and blocks while being named an All-Big 12 honorable mention. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Trump tariffs hitting small business owners in multiple ways
items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Appeals court rules against Trump — again — on California ballots
items.x: ( The Hill ) A split federal appeals court panel again rejected the Trump administration's bid to set aside 20,000 California ballots it says are likely noncitizens until they can be verified. The 2-1 majority on the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit didn’t dispute a lower court’s finding that the list isn’t credible and ruled the administration’s position would undermine the Constitution. “As the district court found—and we discern no clear error—there is no feasible way to identify and segregate the ballots of specific individuals without potentially catastrophic effects on the entire system,” the majority wrote in its unsigned opinion. The majority comprised U.S. Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, an appointee of former President Biden, and U.S. Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, appointed by President Trump. items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Healthcare becomes key midterm issue ahead of policy changes
items.x: (DC BUREAU) – Healthcare costs could rise for insured Americans as states prepare to enforce new Medicaid restrictions in January under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. The legislation, signed by President Donald Trump, requires states to enforce stricter Medicaid work requirements and mandate that enrollees reapply twice a year. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. One dead after crash in front of Farragut Primary School Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. items.t: GM settles $220M lawsuit for allegedly selling private driver data
items.x: HARTFORD, Conn. ( WTNH ) — General Motors has agreed to pay $220 million to settle claims that it illegally sold drivers' private data and location information to third parties. The settlement, announced Thursday, concerns allegations that GM had sold the information to data brokers, who in turn sold it to insurance companies. That private data, in part, was then used to set insurance rates, according to a coalition of attorneys general in 35 states and Washington D.C. “GM turned private vehicles into mobile insurance surveillance machines without consumer consent or awareness," Connecticut Attorney General William Tong said in a Thursday press release announcing the settlement. "GM profited from the sale of this personal driving data, and consumers paid the price in the form of higher premiums." items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. One dead after crash in front of Farragut Primary School A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. items.t: Turn this on to stop hackers from stealing your phone number
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Your phone number is more valuable than you might think. It doesn’t just let people call or text you. It can also be the key to getting into your bank accounts, email and other important services. That’s because so many companies still send two-factor authentication codes by text message. If a hacker takes control of your phone number, they could potentially intercept those codes and use them to break into your accounts, KTLA tech reporter Rich DeMuro explains. The attack is called SIM swapping. It happens when someone tricks your wireless carrier into transferring your phone number to a SIM card or eSIM they control. AT&T, T-Mobile and Verizon all offer free security features designed to help prevent this. The catch? You typically have to turn them on yourself. Here’s exactly how to do it. items.t: Death of ‘Mad Max’ actor Richard Norton linked to peptides, coroner says
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — The death of Australian actor Richard Norton has been linked to injecting unapproved peptides , according to a new coroner's report. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. "Richard had been taking amounts of the medication in excess of the dose prescribed by his medical practitioner. The injection caused an anaphylactic reaction which in turn led to cardiac arrest." Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.x: WASHINGTON, D.C. (NEXSTAR) President Trump says his tariffs are helping the American economy grow but for some small businesses, the math isn't working out. From higher prices to fewer products on store shelves, one Virginia shop is finding ways to adapt. For Ben Knezic, running The Cut Butchery in Alexandria, Virginia – a Washington suburb – means offering customers a little bit of everything. From fresh meats and seafood to imported wines, cheeses and specialty foods, Knezic says Trump's tariffs are making some of those products more expensive. “Just seeing prices on our goods go up and up,” said Knezic. “We've had to raise prices on a lot of things like cheese and wine and some of the other stuff we import." items.t: Why do people still get polio in some countries and not in others?
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Why are people still getting polio in some countries and in not others? – Mia, age 9, Centennial, Colorado On a busy street in Karachi, Pakistan, a healthcare worker kneels down so she’s eye to eye with a toddler. She squeezes two drops of liquid onto the child’s tongue. Then she takes out a purple marker and colors the child’s pinkie fingernail so everyone can see that this toddler is now vaccinated against polio. During big vaccination drives, thousands of health workers like her knock on doors across Pakistan. Most kids in the United States will never experience anything like this, because they get the polio vaccine as a shot at the doctor’s office instead of drops in a door-to-door campaign. items.t: NASA telescope is on the verge of plunging back to Earth after failed rescue mission
items.x: CAPE CANAVERAL, Fla. (AP) — An aging NASA telescope is barely clinging to space after a failed rescue effort left it tottering lower and lower. The U.S. Space Force predicts the Swift Observatory will come crashing down on or around Friday. Most of the 1 ½-ton telescope is expected to burn up in the atmosphere. But a handful of pieces made of denser-than-lead tungsten and some mirror parts could survive reentry, according to NASA's Brad Cenko, the mission’s chief scientist. Any surviving wreckage will most likely plunge into the ocean. But swaths of Africa, Australia, India, Southeast Asia, and Central and South America are within the reentry zone. The Space Force is tracking the telescope’s dwindling path. Its cosmic cremation has the Swift team mourning yet full of gratitude for the observations the telescope made during its 22 years in orbit. Swift blasted off on Nov. 20, 2004, to sea

items.t: How to tell if a car has a rebuilt title
items.x: ( iSeeCars ) A car’s title is a critical document that not only verifies ownership but also reflects a vehicle’s current status and, potentially, any substantial damage or negative conditions it may have suffered in the past. Two common examples are “rebuilt” and “salvage,” terms indicating that a vehicle was previously declared a total loss or met a state's criteria for salvage status. Let’s take a closer look at what circumstances can lead to a rebuilt title status. What is a rebuilt title? A rebuilt title means the car was previously issued a salvage title, usually after being declared a total loss. It was then repaired and met the state's requirements for a rebuilt title, including any required inspections. The damage could have come from a collision, flood, fire, vandalism, or even a theft recovery. A rebuilt brand is meant to be permanent; it never disappears even after flawless re

items.t: How the law protecting Americans from surprise medical bills is driving up healthcare costs
items.x: ( The Conversation ) Imagine you get hit by a car. An ambulance brings you to the nearest hospital. Your private health insurance covers emergency care, but the hospital isn’t in your plan’s network. Before 2022, if you received emergency care from an out-of-network provider or hospital, you could get hit with an extra, often huge bill on top of what you owe as a copay, coinsurance or deductible. A law called the No Surprises Act , which took effect in 2022, was designed to protect people with private health insurance from just these situations. It limits your costs to what you would have paid if the ambulance had brought you to an in-network hospital or you were treated by an in-network provider instead. Many months, a solid chunk of my budget gets spent without me even leaving the house. This is the new “couch economy,” according to a recent report from Visa . In the couch economy era, more and more domestic spending is happening online — 58% in 2026 in the U.S., compared to 48% in 2019, based on Visa transactions. items.t: This is the retirement expense you may be underestimating
items.x: People often underestimate some expenses when planning for retirement. In conversations with older adults about their in-retirement finances, they’ve repeatedly mentioned the cost of dental care. The reasons are straightforward: Our teeth get worse as we age, and yet dental care isn’t covered by Medicare (except for emergency dental procedures for people who are hospitalized). There are three main avenues to covering dental costs during retirement: dental insurance, a Medicare Advantage program that covers dental care, and paying out of pocket. Buying stand-alone dental insurance Older adults can purchase stand-alone dental insurance with monthly premiums typically around $25 to $50. Coverage varies widely, however, with plans typically capping the dollar amounts they’ll cover in a year. items.t: How does daylight saving time impact your health?
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Twice a year, daylight saving time brings a major change to many Americans' schedules, sending clocks back an hour in 48 states. This year, clocks go back an hour on Nov. 1 to standard time. While a 60-minute difference may not seem like much, it has a major impact on many aspects of human life and health. Sleep is impacted, as well as metabolism, mental health and vascular health. Effects can be temporary or long-term. The biannual change has been debated. Dozens of states — and countries — have suggested and pitched legislation for a switch to permanent standard time, which the Society for Research on Biological Rhythms deems "the best option for public health." “The more light exposure you get at the wrong times, the weaker the circadian clock. Norton, 75, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting prescribed but unapproved CJC1295 and ipamorelin, according to multiple reports . "Richard's death was triggered by his injection of the peptide CJC1295/Ipamorelin," the report reads. Norton was known for his role in "Mad Max: Fury Road," "The Octagon," and more, as well as his martial arts scenes with heavyweights of the genre, such as Jackie Chan and Chuck Norris. items.t: Unexplained weight gain and 6 common health problems that can cause it
items.x: Unexplained weight gain, meaning pounds that pile on without any change in diet or activity, often comes from a handful of common health problems. These include an underactive thyroid, polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome, heart failure, kidney disease, depression and Cushing’s syndrome. Some of them add fat by changing hormones and metabolism. Others add weight through fluid the body cannot clear. The American Heart Association says people with heart failure should call a doctor if they gain more than 2 to 3 pounds in a day or 5 pounds in a week. Normal daily swings of a few pounds usually come from water and food. The weight worth questioning is the kind that keeps climbing for weeks with no clear reason. googletag.cmd.push(function() { var mapping_lb_1 = googletag.sizeMapping() .addSize([1084, 0], [[300, 250]]) .addSize([0, 0], [[300, 250]]) .build(); googletag.defineSlot('2208318

Customers with questions may contact Dorchester County Water and Sewer Department Customer Service at 843-832-0075 or 843-563-0075.

items.t: Man sustains ‘potentially serious injuries’ during camper fire in Burton
items.x: BURTON, S.C. (WCSC) — A man sustained “potentially serious injuries” during a camper fire in Burton on Saturday morning. Multiple departments responded to the fire on Baynard Road around 8 a.m. Neighbors reported that a camper, where two people were living, was on fire with the residents still possibly inside and multiple propane tanks nearby. Fire crews arrived on scene to find a camper almost fully engulfed. One adult male had been pulled free by a neighbor and had sustained “potentially serious injuries,” the Burton Fire District stated. With reports of possibly one more person inside, Burton firefighters entered the camper to perform a search and found no one else inside. The injured resident was treated by Beaufort County EMS personnel and transported to Beaufort Memorial Hospital. Firefighters quickly extinguished the fire. No other injuries were reported.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

Most of those people live in urban areas, where fast food and convenience shops replace healthy, nutritious foods as the most affordable option. Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. In Michigan, organizations like the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network are advocating for urban farming and food sovereignty. Chris Borick, a political science professor at Lehigh University, said AI has become a major issue in several races in the last few months. He noted how different the rhetoric surrounding it has been compared to other new technologies. “We like tech traditionally as part of our political economy. That’s really changed in the last year, where you see a much more neutral and sometimes negative political position on AI,” Borick said. items.t: South Carolina early voting tops 800,000, sets pace for midterm record
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WCSC) — South Carolina is on pace to shatter its previous midterm early voting record, with more than 830,000 ballots already cast ahead of Election Day. According to the South Carolina Election Commission, turnout has far exceeded the pace seen during the 2022 midterm election cycle. Election Commission Executive Director Conway Belangia said turnout is already roughly double what the state saw four years ago and expects strong participation through the final days of early voting. “It is probably double what we saw four years ago, and we still have two solid days, and we know that Friday and Saturday will always be big turnout days just because it’s the last two days,” Belangia said. items.t: Trump to make final midterm stops in Iowa and Kansas Sunday
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - President Donald Trump will make final campaign stops in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday, two days before Tuesday’s midterm elections. Trump won Iowa three times and Kansas twice. He is hoping to give Republicans a final boost in both states. He originally scrapped the stops but decided at the last minute to go through with them. The Senate seats in both states are a must-win for Republicans to hold the chamber. A recent Marist poll shows Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson trailing Democrat Josh Turek by three points in Iowa. In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton holds a narrow lead over incumbent Republican Roger Marshall for the first time. House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said he is not worried. “I’ve seen the voters on the ground. I’m telling you, the polls are wrong. They’re inaccurate. items.t: More than 42 million Americans have cast early midterm ballots
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - More than 42 million Americans have cast midterm ballots, and interesting demographic data shows who is voting. According to the University of Florida Election Lab , early midterm turnout is similar to the 2018 “blue wave.” The lab said enthusiasm appears to be on the Democrats’ side. Michael McDonald, a University of Florida political scientist, said the U.S. could be headed toward record turnout. “It’s possible that we will beat the 2018 turnout rate. That was the highest turnout rate for midterm elections since 1914. But there are uneven patterns of turnout,” McDonald said. McDonald said the uneven turnout levels come from a partisan divide. “Registered Democrats, unaffiliated, those people who don’t have a party registration, are engaged at the moment. items.x: NORTH CHARLESTON, S.C. (WCSC) — The nonprofit Lily Pad: A Soft Place to Land and the South Carolina Department of Social Services on Friday cut the ribbon on six trauma-informed rooms for children entering foster care at the Charleston County DSS office. items.t: S.C. law requires Child Abuse Protocol with no penalty for ignoring it
items.x: CHARLESTON, S.C. (WCSC) — With the Lowcountry seeing numerous cases of parents or caregivers being charged with child abuse or neglect over the last several months, the laws that best protect these children and how agencies respond to the calls are getting a closer look. When agencies work together to best respond to a case about potential child abuse, neglect, or exploitation, they are required by state law to follow the Child Abuse Response Protocol. But that same state law also says an agency won’t face any consequences if it doesn’t do it. “It indicates that law enforcement is going to have its own internal policy,” defense attorney Stephan Futeral said while looking over the law. He also acknowledges it is possible that an agency might not even have its own policy. items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

Investigators allege she targeted animals carrying high financial pledges raised by social media donors trying to save shelter pets from euthanasia. items.x: BEND, Ore. ( KPTV /Gray News) - A teacher who fought with the gunman during a deadly school shooting earlier this month in Oregon has released her first statement since that tragic day. items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.
