items.t: Three pedestrians, including two children, injured in London crash
items.x: LONDON, Ky. (WKYT) - Three pedestrians, including two children, were hospitalized Saturday evening after being struck by a car in London, according to police. The London Police Department reported that emergency dispatch received a call at around 7:05 p.m. regarding a vehicle that struck multiple pedestrians on Middleground Way, just off South Highway 25. Responding officers found that a white Toyota Camry had struck an adult and two kids. All three victims suffered non-life-threatening injuries and were transported by Laurel County Ambulance to a local hospital for evaluation and treatment. Emergency personnel have since cleared the area, and Middleground Way has fully reopened to traffic. Police said the collision remains under investigation, and further details will be provided as they become available.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. ( KSLA /Gray News) - A former high school band director facing dozens of sex offense charges is in critical condition after shooting himself during an arrest Thursday, authorities said. Bossier Parish Sheriff’s deputies were serving an arrest warrant for 56-year-old Kevin Williams at his Bossier City home when he resisted, according to officials. During a physical struggle, Williams pulled a handgun from his waistband and shot himself. Deputies immediately administered first aid until emergency medical personnel arrived. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: Daylight saving time ends Sunday: How the time change can impact your mental health
items.x: HARRISONBURG, Va. (WHSV) - As daylight saving time comes to an end early Sunday morning, standard time returns — bringing earlier sunsets, shorter days, and an extra hour of sleep. For many, the annual time shift brings more than just a schedule adjustment. It can trigger feelings of sluggishness, fatigue, and noticeable dips in mood. Holly Humphreys, a licensed professional counselor with Thriveworks, said the shift often disrupts the body’s circadian rhythm, or internal biological clock. “With the daylight hours getting shorter and it getting darker earlier, I do typically see a decline in my clients’ moods around this time of year,” Humphreys said. “Some don’t stay. items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: AAA warns of increased safety risks during Halloween and time change
items.x: HARRISONBURG, Va. (WHSV) - With Halloween falling on a Saturday this year, AAA said that could mean more people on the road late at night. When you add in the end of daylight saving time and the earlier sunset, drivers, pedestrians and partygoers all face added risks. items.t: How AI is impacting the midterm elections

items.t: Halloween comes knocking at UVA Health Children’s, bringing joy to young patients
items.x: CHARLOTTESVILLE, Va. (WVIR) - Halloween usually means putting on a costume, grabbing a bag and heading out to collect candy. But for children spending the holiday in the hospital, trick-or-treating can look a little different. At UVA Health Children’s, an annual tradition is turning trick-or-treating upside down, bringing costumes, treats and special visitors directly to young patients who cannot celebrate the holiday at home. For Samantha Butler, whose 8-year-old daughter, Kaylee Heflin, is hospitalized at UVA Health Children’s, the celebration meant more than a few Halloween treats. “I can’t express to you how much it makes me feel as a mother to have my daughter included on little acts like this, like Halloween,” Butler said. According to Virginia State Police, Jeffrey Scott Bennett was last seen at his residence around 8:30 a.m. Thursday, Oct. 29. Police believe Bennett may be traveling near the Blue Ridge Parkway in the Staunton area. He may be driving a green 1995 Toyota T100 pickup truck with Virginia license plate XGG8878. items.t: New Market man dies after Rockingham County motorcycle crash
items.x: ROCKINGHAM COUNTY, Va. (WHSV) - A New Market man died Thursday after a motorcycle crash in Rockingham County, according to Virginia State Police. The crash happened Thursday at 10:35 a.m. at the intersection of Spotswood Trail and New Hope Road, involving a 2018 Yamaha motorcycle and a 2026 Toyota pickup truck, according to VSP. The motorcycle was traveling east on Spotswood Trail at a “high rate of speed,” VSP said, when the Toyota pickup tried to cross Spotswood Trail from New Hope Road. The motorcycle hit the side of the pickup, and the rider was ejected into the median, VSP said. VSP identified the motorcyclist as Xavier Smith, 22, of New Market. Smith was taken to Sentara RMH Medical Center, where he was pronounced dead. The driver and passenger of the pickup, who VSP said were both from Pawleys Island, South Carolina, were not injured. VSP continues to investigate the crash.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Affordability remains the main talking point ahead of the 2026 midterms, and food accessibility is one issue voters may consider when heading to the polls. It’s estimated around 53 million Americans live in what’s called a “food desert,” lower-income areas without easy access to supermarkets or grocery stores. Most of those people live in urban areas, where fast food and convenience shops replace healthy, nutritious foods as the most affordable option. Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. In Michigan, organizations like the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network are advocating for urban farming and food sovereignty. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

Most of those people live in urban areas, where fast food and convenience shops replace healthy, nutritious foods as the most affordable option. Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. Hinojosa has served as the State Representative for Austin since 2016. She says now is the time to get Texas “back to basics”, and oust Governor Abbott, who is running for his fourth term. Waste and vendor contracts Hinojosa said waste, fraud and abuse exist in state government, but not among civil servants. “We need to essentially ‘DOGE’ the Texas government. It is in all of these vendor contracts that have amassed under Greg Abbott,” Hinojosa said. DOGE is a reference to the U.S. Department of Government Efficiency. items.t: Experts eye key voting blocs ahead of Midterms
items.x: NEW YORK CITY (Gray Media) - With millions of ballots already cast ahead of Election Day, conversations surrounding voter turnout are intensifying. Rather than looking solely at party affiliation, political insiders are closely watching three specific demographic groups that could ultimately decide which party controls Congress. Lincoln Mitchell, a political analyst and professor at Columbia University, says the first group feeling pressure is rural voters. Economic headwinds, including agricultural tariffs and the rising cost of everyday essentials like home heating and diesel, are pinching household budgets in rural communities. While Mitchell does not expect these voters to dramatically flip parties, financial strain could depress turnout or weaken enthusiasm for Republicans and President Donald Trump. items.t: How AI is impacting the midterm elections
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As midterm candidates begin to make their final pitches to voters, experts are speaking out about the impact of artificial intelligence on this election cycle. Chris Borick, a political science professor at Lehigh University, said AI has become a major issue in several races in the last few months. He noted how different the rhetoric surrounding it has been compared to other new technologies. “We like tech traditionally as part of our political economy. That’s really changed in the last year, where you see a much more neutral and sometimes negative political position on AI,” Borick said. items.t: Trump to make final midterm stops in Iowa and Kansas Sunday
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - President Donald Trump will make final campaign stops in Iowa and Kansas on Sunday, two days before Tuesday’s midterm elections. Trump won Iowa three times and Kansas twice. He is hoping to give Republicans a final boost in both states. He originally scrapped the stops but decided at the last minute to go through with them. The Senate seats in both states are a must-win for Republicans to hold the chamber. A recent Marist poll shows Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson trailing Democrat Josh Turek by three points in Iowa. In Kansas, Democrat Adam Hamilton holds a narrow lead over incumbent Republican Roger Marshall for the first time. House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said he is not worried. “I’ve seen the voters on the ground. I’m telling you, the polls are wrong. They’re inaccurate. items.t: More than 42 million Americans have cast early midterm ballots
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - More than 42 million Americans have cast midterm ballots, and interesting demographic data shows who is voting. According to the University of Florida Election Lab , early midterm turnout is similar to the 2018 “blue wave.” The lab said enthusiasm appears to be on the Democrats’ side. Michael McDonald, a University of Florida political scientist, said the U.S. could be headed toward record turnout. “It’s possible that we will beat the 2018 turnout rate. That was the highest turnout rate for midterm elections since 1914. But there are uneven patterns of turnout,” McDonald said. McDonald said the uneven turnout levels come from a partisan divide. “Registered Democrats, unaffiliated, those people who don’t have a party registration, are engaged at the moment. President Donald Trump launched the war with one major objective: preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. Earlier in the war, the president gave additional reasons for military action against Iran. items.t: The relationship between Christian nationalism and Americans’ views of democracy
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The number of Americans who identify with Christian nationalism is slightly declining, but religion remains a large part of politics for both candidates and voters ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. “We see where Americans fall on this spectrum of Christian nationalism, which really tells us a lot about what they think democracy is and how it’s functioning,” said Andrew Whitehead , a professor of sociology at Indiana University Indianapolis and a research fellow for the Charles F. Kettering Foundation. Whitehead cited data from the Kettering Foundation and Gallup’s annual national survey of more than 23,000 adults. items.x: LUBBOCK, Texas (KCBD) - A former Lubbock nurse has been found guilty of reckless bodily injury that led to a 4-month-old’s death. In January 2023, Fraher, 71, a former licensed vocational nurse, was taking care of a 4-month-old special needs child who required a ventilator. Prosecutors say the baby suffered a respiratory emergency while Fraher was changing her diaper. Investigators say Fraher ignored the ventilator alarms and failed to provide medical care. The baby was taken to the hospital, where she died eight days later. Fraher will go before Judge Douglas Freitag for sentencing where she faces up to 20 years in prison. items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.x: JONESVILLE, Fla. ( WCJB /Gray News) — A 1-year-old boy was hit and killed on a Florida roadway, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. items.t: Man posing as Amazon delivery driver accused of stealing multiple packages from neighborhood
items.x: LAKE OSWEGO, Ore. ( KPTV /Gray News) - A Portland man has been arrested after police say he stole packages while posing as an Amazon delivery driver. According to the Lake Oswego Police Department, 51-year-old Ramiro Despaigne Rodriguez was arrested on Oct. 21 after packages were reported stolen from at least eight homes in the Lake Oswego area. Police said the suspect was caught on surveillance video driving a car marked with a “delivery driver” sticker and wearing an Amazon vest. Rodriguez was arrested and booked into the Clackamas County Jail, where he faces first-degree theft charges. Investigators believe there may be more victims connected to this case.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. items.x: LOUDENDALE, W.Va. (WSAZ) - A fire happening around 7:00 a.m. on the 100 block of Cecil Drive in Loudendale, Saturday, killed two pets, as well as the house being deemed a total loss, according to the Chief of the Loudendale Volunteer Fire Department. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

Dillenburg, who operated Welcome Home Canine Rescue out of her residence, has been charged with torture or mutilation of a vertebrate animal, a felony, and fraud. Court documents stated Dillenburg pulled 21 dogs from Indianapolis Animal Care Services over a 10-day period in late April. Investigators allege she targeted animals carrying high financial pledges raised by social media donors trying to save shelter pets from euthanasia. If you think tossing a couple gutter balls in a row sounds scary, at Casey’s Lanes in Grayson, they’re upping the fear ante. Rebecca McKinney and her husband acquired the bowling alley four years ago, and this year for the first time, every Friday and Saturday night in October, part of their space that’s normally a skating rink converts into the Haunted Alley. Part of the proceeds last weekend went to the East Carter High School wrestling team. items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: Detroit organization promotes urban farming amid food insecurity
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Affordability remains the main talking point ahead of the 2026 midterms, and food accessibility is one issue voters may consider when heading to the polls. It’s estimated around 53 million Americans live in what’s called a “food desert,” lower-income areas without easy access to supermarkets or grocery stores. Most of those people live in urban areas, where fast food and convenience shops replace healthy, nutritious foods as the most affordable option. Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. In Michigan, organizations like the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network are advocating for urban farming and food sovereignty. items.t: Experts eye key voting blocs ahead of Midterms
items.x: NEW YORK CITY (Gray Media) - With millions of ballots already cast ahead of Election Day, conversations surrounding voter turnout are intensifying. Rather than looking solely at party affiliation, political insiders are closely watching three specific demographic groups that could ultimately decide which party controls Congress. Economic headwinds, including agricultural tariffs and the rising cost of everyday essentials like home heating and diesel, are pinching household budgets in rural communities. While Mitchell does not expect these voters to dramatically flip parties, financial strain could depress turnout or weaken enthusiasm for Republicans and President Donald Trump. items.t: How AI is impacting the midterm elections
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As midterm candidates begin to make their final pitches to voters, experts are speaking out about the impact of artificial intelligence on this election cycle. Chris Borick, a political science professor at Lehigh University, said AI has become a major issue in several races in the last few months. He noted how different the rhetoric surrounding it has been compared to other new technologies. “We like tech traditionally as part of our political economy. That’s really changed in the last year, where you see a much more neutral and sometimes negative political position on AI,” Borick said. items.t: More than 42 million Americans have cast early midterm ballots

items.t: Hometown Hero | Heidi Greenleaf
items.x: ASHLAND, Ky. (WSAZ) - A little greenhouse in Ashland is growing more than just plants. A woman’s love for greenery has turned into a way for neighbors to connect, share and find a little peace in their everyday lives. For owner Heidi Greenleaf, our latest Hometown Hero, it all started with a house full of plants and a simple question. “I thought, how can I share this with other people?” she said. “So, I decided to pop up a free community exchange, very similar to those little free book libraries. items.t: Courthouse weddings feature Halloween theme
items.x: HUNTINGTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) - Normally, people want their wedding days filled with light colors, a white dress, and flower centerpieces. Some people, though, like to live on the spookier side. On Friday, couples who have a fondness for the Halloween season came to Cabell County Circuit Judge Chad Lovejoy in Huntington to officiate their special day on the holiday. These couples ditched a traditional wedding for one with black tablecloths, a pumpkin balloon, and an orange and black color scheme. “What we do is very, very serious, and so having a day like this, that the community can come in and have a wedding and have some fun and smile is a nice,” Judge Lovejoy said. “It’s one of the nice things that we do.” Judge Lovejoy and his staff really got into the fun, decorating the courtroom for the big day. Altogether, including walkups, they performed about a dozen Halloween weddings on Friday.

items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.t: More than a game: The WWII bond that forever linked Notre Dame and Navy
items.x: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - The Notre Dame Fighting Irish and the Navy Midshipmen first met on the football field in 1927, starting a tradition that has now lasted nearly a century. Ninety-eight matchups later, playing through World Wars and 18 American presidencies, it has become one of the longest unbroken rivalries in all of college football. “The history of it, the why, you know, it goes way back with the war and the agreement between presidents,” Notre Dame head coach Marcus Freeman said. Since 2011, the teams have played for the Rip Miller Trophy, named after Edgar “Rip” Miller, a former Irish player under the legendary Knute Rockne and a former Navy head coach. The unique prize has two symmetric halves. Each team holds its side, which is inscribed with the team’s captains for that year. The two pieces reunite annually for the rivalry matchup. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: Detroit organization promotes urban farming amid food insecurity
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Affordability remains the main talking point ahead of the 2026 midterms, and food accessibility is one issue voters may consider when heading to the polls. It’s estimated around 53 million Americans live in what’s called a “food desert,” lower-income areas without easy access to supermarkets or grocery stores. Most of those people live in urban areas, where fast food and convenience shops replace healthy, nutritious foods as the most affordable option. Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. In Michigan, organizations like the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network are advocating for urban farming and food sovereignty. items.t: South Bend’s MLK Dream Center unveils new mural
items.x: SOUTH BEND, Ind. (WNDU) - A new mural was unveiled in South Bend’s MLK Dream Center on Friday! The city of South Bend teamed up with the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi Indians and its Four Winds Casinos to unveil the art inside the Dream Center’s gym. The mural displays woodland flowers and the Medicine Wheel, which are native to the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi’s ancestral homelands. The flowers have cultural significance in Potawatomi traditions. They serve as a resource for traditional medicine, markers for planting and harvesting seasons and elements of teaching and ceremonies, according to a news release. The design also weaves in the center’s bright colors and inspirational phrases like “dream it, believe it, achieve it,” underscoring the partnership’s goal of giving people of all ages a place to learn, grow and chase their dreams. items.x: NEW YORK CITY (Gray Media) - With millions of ballots already cast ahead of Election Day, conversations surrounding voter turnout are intensifying. Rather than looking solely at party affiliation, political insiders are closely watching three specific demographic groups that could ultimately decide which party controls Congress. Economic headwinds, including agricultural tariffs and the rising cost of everyday essentials like home heating and diesel, are pinching household budgets in rural communities. While Mitchell does not expect these voters to dramatically flip parties, financial strain could depress turnout or weaken enthusiasm for Republicans and President Donald Trump. items.t: How AI is impacting the midterm elections
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As midterm candidates begin to make their final pitches to voters, experts are speaking out about the impact of artificial intelligence on this election cycle. Chris Borick, a political science professor at Lehigh University, said AI has become a major issue in several races in the last few months. He noted how different the rhetoric surrounding it has been compared to other new technologies. “We like tech traditionally as part of our political economy. That’s really changed in the last year, where you see a much more neutral and sometimes negative political position on AI,” Borick said. items.t: Amish Acres owner arrested in Louisiana on felony warrant
items.x: NAPPANEE, Ind. (WNDU) - The owner of the historic Amish Acres property was arrested Thursday in Louisiana on a felony warrant for issuing worthless checks, according to records. Records show 52-year-old Michael Bradley Loftin, who goes by Brad Juneau, was arrested in Louisiana. A judge ordered him held without bond. The arrest comes more than two months after the state fire marshal shut Amish Acres down over severe fire safety violations . The Indiana Department of Homeland Security released a new report two days later stating that no violations were found at Amish Acres . items.t: More than 42 million Americans have cast early midterm ballots
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - More than 42 million Americans have cast midterm ballots, and interesting demographic data shows who is voting. According to the University of Florida Election Lab , early midterm turnout is similar to the 2018 “blue wave.” The lab said enthusiasm appears to be on the Democrats’ side. Michael McDonald, a University of Florida political scientist, said the U.S. could be headed toward record turnout. “It’s possible that we will beat the 2018 turnout rate. That was the highest turnout rate for midterm elections since 1914. But there are uneven patterns of turnout,” McDonald said. McDonald said the uneven turnout levels come from a partisan divide. “Registered Democrats, unaffiliated, those people who don’t have a party registration, are engaged at the moment. items.t: Buchanan first responders offer Halloween candy checks

Buchanan first responders have a high-tech solution. “I always encourage for them to then go downtown … to have their candy checked, because you just never know nowadays,” said Buchanan resident Daleen Granger. Court records show Christopher Hochstetler entered the plea agreement this week. An attempted murder charge was dismissed as part of the agreement. According to charging documents, Hochstetler told police he really didn’t like his mom when asked why he set the house on fire. Investigators said Hochstetler used a candle lighter and rolled-up toilet paper to start the fire. He placed it next to a wood log in front of his mother’s bedroom, according to the documents. Statewide, 97 cases have been reported, including 22 in LaGrange County and three in Elkhart County. Measles is one of the most contagious illnesses. items.t: Berrien County dentist reaches plea agreement in staff sexual misconduct case
items.x: BERRIEN COUNTY, Mich. (WNDU) - A Berrien County dentist accused of sexually touching his staff has reached a plea agreement. Officials said Charles Howenstine, the former owner of St. Joseph Dentistry, pleaded no contest Thursday, Oct. 29, to one felony count of seduction and two counts of assault and battery. The seduction charge carries up to five years in prison. In Michigan, a no contest plea does not admit guilt. Under state law, it means the defendant is not going to fight the state’s case. According to charging paperwork, the victims, who were dental assistants at St. Joseph Dentistry, gave multiple examples of sexual misconduct, saying Howenstine would regularly touch their buttocks. Another victim reported that Howenstine grazed their thigh while they were treating a patient. Howenstine is scheduled to be sentenced Dec. 7. items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. In 2024, Virzi was visiting Pittsburgh to assist her longtime friend, Savannah Roberts, with newborn twins Leon and Ari Katz, NBC News reported. When the parents took Ari to a hospital to treat unexplained injuries, Virzi offered to watch Leon. Later that night, Virzi called 911 claiming Leon fell from a baby bouncer. He was rushed to a children’s hospital, where he died. Plus, we meet a 91-year-old world record holder in track and field proving that staying active has no age limit. items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.t: 2 people, 5 dogs rescued from Olive Branch house fire
items.x: OLIVE BRANCH, Miss. (WMC) - Two people and five dogs were rescued Thursday night after a house fire broke out along Oak Leaf Drive. The Olive Branch Fire Department responded to the home around 7 p.m. When crews arrived, they helped an elderly woman and two dogs safely evacuate. The woman was transported to a local hospital for evaluation. Firefighters then entered the home, encountering heavy smoke and flames spreading through the kitchen and living room. During a search, crews located a elderly man trapped inside a back bathroom. He was rushed to Regional One Health and treated for smoke inhalation and esophageal burns; officials expect him to make a full recovery. Firefighters also found three more dogs inside the house, rescuing and treating them on scene. Investigators determined the fire started in the kitchen, though the exact cause remains under investigation. Click here to sign

items.t: Mount Olive hosts annual Scarecrow Festival

They walked through downtown getting candy and prizes as part of Mount Olive’s annual Scarecrow Festival. The family-friendly event featured trick-or-treating and lots of games for children. items.t: Southern Miss defeats ULM 35-21 in Louisiana
items.x: MONROE, La. (WDAM) - The Golden Eagles (3-5, 2-2 Sun Belt) beat UL Monroe (1-7, 1-3 Sun Belt) 35-21 in a Sun Belt matchup in Louisiana. This is USM’s second win in a row, after last week’s thrilling match against Louisiana-Lafayette. Steven Robinson and Jamarice Wilder each ran for more than 100 yards and combined for three touchdowns. Robinson ran for 151 yards on 21 carries that included a 33-yard touchdown run. Wilder finished with 104 on 15 carries and scored on a 21-yard run early in the third quarter and added a 21-yarder with 1:52 remaining. Landry Lyddy was 15-of-30 passing for 130 yards with a touchdown pass for Southern Miss (3-5, 2-2 Sun Belt), which has won two straight after a five-game skid. Southern Miss hosts James Madison next on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 7 p.m. Want more WDAM 7 news in your inbox? Click here to subscribe to our newsletter.

items.t: 1-year-old boy dies after walking into road by home, troopers say
items.x: JONESVILLE, Fla. ( WCJB /Gray News) — A 1-year-old boy was hit and killed on a Florida roadway, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened in the Jonesville area Friday afternoon. Investigators said a car was headed west on Newberry Road when the boy entered the road from a nearby home. The driver didn’t see the child and hit him. The 1-year-old was taken to the hospital, where he died. Further information was not available.

items.t: Man posing as Amazon delivery driver accused of stealing multiple packages from neighborhood
items.x: LAKE OSWEGO, Ore. ( KPTV /Gray News) - A Portland man has been arrested after police say he stole packages while posing as an Amazon delivery driver. According to the Lake Oswego Police Department, 51-year-old Ramiro Despaigne Rodriguez was arrested on Oct. 21 after packages were reported stolen from at least eight homes in the Lake Oswego area. Police said the suspect was caught on surveillance video driving a car marked with a “delivery driver” sticker and wearing an Amazon vest. Rodriguez was arrested and booked into the Clackamas County Jail, where he faces first-degree theft charges. Investigators believe there may be more victims connected to this case.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

Investigators allege she targeted animals carrying high financial pledges raised by social media donors trying to save shelter pets from euthanasia. items.x: (Gray News) - Kyle Chrisley, son of reality television star Todd Chrisley, has pleaded guilty to resisting arrest in an incident from December 2025. items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

Chrisley was arrested on charges including assault on a police officer, disorderly conduct, domestic assault, public intoxication and resisting arrest. items.x: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WVLT) - Knoxville Police are attempting to find Kaylecia Woodard, 34, who was last seen on Friday afternoon, according to the TBI and KPD. The TBI has since issued a Silver Alert for Woodard. Knoxville police say was last seen leaving her home in the 2900 block of Lay Avenue at around 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 30. Woodard is 5’4 and 150 lbs. She was last seen wearing a multi-colored shirt, white pants and a red backpack, KPD says. She was pictured in an unknown red Sedan that is possibly traveling towards Kentucky. She has multiple health conditions that could affect her ability to return home safely, KPD says. Police urge those with information concerning her whereabouts to contact 911. The TBI also urges the public to contact them at 1-800-TBI-FIND. This is a developing story.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

Most of those people live in urban areas, where fast food and convenience shops replace healthy, nutritious foods as the most affordable option. Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. In Michigan, organizations like the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network are advocating for urban farming and food sovereignty. items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we address how aging and illness can impact intimacy, sharing practical ways for couples to talk openly and safely navigate sex after a diagnosis. Plus, we meet a 91-year-old world record holder in track and field proving that staying active has no age limit. items.t: 91-year-old track and field world record holder continues to compete
items.x: SHELBURNE, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — Flo Meiler began competing in track and field at age 60. She is now 91 and holds two world records, in the pole vault and triple jump. Medals fill Meiler’s home in Shelburne. Most are gold, and a few are silver. How she started Meiler began competing at 60 when her friend Barbara Jordan convinced her to try the long jump at the Vermont Senior Games, and Meiler was hooked. Jordan died a decade ago. “I miss her so much,” Meiler said. Still competing at 91 Meiler continues to compete. “I’m sad that I can’t jump like I used to, but I really enjoy it,” she said. Meiler said it lifts her up when other athletes approach her and tell her she inspires them. “I really feel really warm inside because I’ve had so many athletes come up to me and say, ‘What an inspiration you have been to me,’” she said. “That’s a wonderful feeling.” Inspiring others One of the people

items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - The Chatham County Sheriff’s Office parking lot was decked out in all things Halloween for this year’s Fall Festival. Tables were covered in food and candy as music filled the space. They also held a free book giveaway and had bouncy houses for the kids. items.t: ILA Local 1414 hosts Halloween event to create safe space for families
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - The International Longshoremen’s Association Local 1414’s President Paul Mosley Sr. said Saturday’s Halloween event was about creating a safe environment for the kids to enjoy the day. Chatham County Sheriff Richard Coleman was also at the event before attending the CCSO Fall Festival, and shared similar thoughts about providing a space for families to safely get candy and gather on Halloween. “The community is always going to be the key. items.t: 3 injured after Halloween morning shooting in Savannah
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WTOC) - Three people were injured after an early morning shooting in Savannah. Savannah Police say officers responded to a shooting at West Bryan Street and Martin Luther King Jr. Blvd around 2:30 am. on Halloween morning. Officials say three people were found and treated on scene when police arrived. Two victims were taken to the hospital for further treatment. No arrests have been made, and the investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information is asked to contact CrimeStoppers at 912-234-2020, or submit an anonymous tip through the SPD mobile app.

items.t: Man posing as Amazon delivery driver accused of stealing multiple packages from neighborhood
items.x: LAKE OSWEGO, Ore. ( KPTV /Gray News) - A Portland man has been arrested after police say he stole packages while posing as an Amazon delivery driver. According to the Lake Oswego Police Department, 51-year-old Ramiro Despaigne Rodriguez was arrested on Oct. 21 after packages were reported stolen from at least eight homes in the Lake Oswego area. Police said the suspect was caught on surveillance video driving a car marked with a “delivery driver” sticker and wearing an Amazon vest. Rodriguez was arrested and booked into the Clackamas County Jail, where he faces first-degree theft charges. Investigators believe there may be more victims connected to this case.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

Butler authorities say Kayla Dillenburg, 30, strangled a dog she pulled from an Indianapolis shelter, profited from donor pledges meant for its care, and admitted to the killing on a recorded phone call. Dillenburg, who operated Welcome Home Canine Rescue out of her residence, has been charged with torture or mutilation of a vertebrate animal, a felony, and fraud. Court documents stated Dillenburg pulled 21 dogs from Indianapolis Animal Care Services over a 10-day period in late April. Investigators allege she targeted animals carrying high financial pledges raised by social media donors trying to save shelter pets from euthanasia. items.t: Kyle Chrisley pleads guilty to charges stemming from 2025 arrest, reports say
items.x: (Gray News) - Kyle Chrisley, son of reality television star Todd Chrisley, has pleaded guilty to resisting arrest in an incident from December 2025. Chrisley was arrested on charges including assault on a police officer, disorderly conduct, domestic assault, public intoxication and resisting arrest. According to Us Magazine , the remaining charges were dismissed. items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

We’re keeping a close eye on a cold front moving in next week that could bring some showers to Election Day before it arrives. This front looks to move through Tuesday night into Wednesday morning, bringing a round of rain and storms. Some of those storms could turn strong to severe, which would be our first significant severe weather threat of the season. items.t: 1-year-old boy dies after walking into road by home, troopers say
items.x: JONESVILLE, Fla. ( WCJB /Gray News) — A 1-year-old boy was hit and killed on a Florida roadway, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The crash happened in the Jonesville area Friday afternoon. Investigators said a car was headed west on Newberry Road when the boy entered the road from a nearby home. The driver didn’t see the child and hit him. The 1-year-old was taken to the hospital, where he died. Further information was not available.

items.x: CLEVELAND, Ohio ( WOIO /Gray News) — An ambulance driver is accused of abandoning a patient he was transporting to the hospital earlier this week in Ohio. The incident happened Wednesday evening in Cleveland. The patient was being transported to the Cleveland Clinic with chest pain when the ambulance driver got lost, told her he was done driving for the day, and called an Uber to take him home. The driver worked for Lynx EMS, a private ambulance company, and not for Cleveland EMS. According to Cleveland Association of Rescue Employees (CARE) Local 1975, once the driver left the patient, a Cleveland EMS unit responded to the scene. The paramedics then administered medical care and brought the woman to the hospital, a CARE spokesperson said in a statement . “We stand by our EMTs, paramedics and dispatchers who strive to provide the best care to anyone who is in need of it,” the CARE spokes

items.t: ‘I Voted’ sticker creator talks about how it started
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - The “I Voted” sticker given to people who cast ballots began with one woman, Janet Boudreau, who designed it after seeing a local county hand out a different sticker on Election Day. Boudreau said she has long supported voting, which she described as the right and duty of American citizens to share their voice. “This is the one day that we have to amplify what we want our world to look like, and it just irritated me and my folks, too, when people would say, oh I forgot the election,” Boudreau said. In 1987, Boudreau owned an election supply and voting equipment company. She noticed a county in Washington state had started handing out stickers on Election Day. “It was black and white and had an X in a square. And that’s it. items.t: Suspect in New Orleans gas station death deliberately ran over victim twice, court records say
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - A Marrero woman accused of a fatal hit-and-run at a St. Roch-area gas station deliberately ran over her victim twice after stealing her goods, according to an investigation detailed in court records. The account of 54-year-old victim Erica Gabriel’s death was provided in a booking report for suspect Shira Barousse Northcutt obtained Saturday (Oct. 31) by Fox 8. Northcutt, 44, was booked into the Orleans Justice Center jail Friday afternoon on counts of hit-and-run causing death and obstruction of justice-evidence tampering. The report said Northcutt turned herself in Friday morning to New Orleans police. She said her vehicle was with her brother, would not say where, and would not provide any further statement without an attorney present, the report said. According to the document, Gabriel and Northcutt were inside the Brothers Gas Station at 3101 Elysian Fields Ave.

items.t: Man posing as Amazon delivery driver accused of stealing multiple packages from neighborhood
items.x: LAKE OSWEGO, Ore. ( KPTV /Gray News) - A Portland man has been arrested after police say he stole packages while posing as an Amazon delivery driver. According to the Lake Oswego Police Department, 51-year-old Ramiro Despaigne Rodriguez was arrested on Oct. 21 after packages were reported stolen from at least eight homes in the Lake Oswego area. Police said the suspect was caught on surveillance video driving a car marked with a “delivery driver” sticker and wearing an Amazon vest. Rodriguez was arrested and booked into the Clackamas County Jail, where he faces first-degree theft charges. Investigators believe there may be more victims connected to this case.

items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

Dillenburg, who operated Welcome Home Canine Rescue out of her residence, has been charged with torture or mutilation of a vertebrate animal, a felony, and fraud. Court documents stated Dillenburg pulled 21 dogs from Indianapolis Animal Care Services over a 10-day period in late April. Investigators allege she targeted animals carrying high financial pledges raised by social media donors trying to save shelter pets from euthanasia. items.t: Tulane rallies from 10-point deficit, beats Charlotte in OT, 38-31

(AP) — Johnnie Daniels had 99 yards rushing and two touchdowns, TJ Smith returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown and Tulane rallied from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat Charlotte in overtime, 38-31, on Friday night (Oct. 30). Short-yardage quarterback Dagan Bruno lunged for a short TD on fourth-and-goal on the first possession in overtime. Charlotte a first-and-goal at the 4, but after two short runs yielded just 1 yard, Conner Harrell threw back-to-back incomplete passes to end it. Derrick Eley had a 1-yard rushing TD that gave Charlotte a 31-21 lead with 10:52 remaining in the fourth quarter. Cooper Helmke made a 27-yard field goal about 4½ minutes later and Trace Johnson threw an 11-yard touchdown pass to Bredell Richardson with 10 seconds left that tied the game 31-31. items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: Detroit organization promotes urban farming amid food insecurity
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - Affordability remains the main talking point ahead of the 2026 midterms, and food accessibility is one issue voters may consider when heading to the polls. It’s estimated around 53 million Americans live in what’s called a “food desert,” lower-income areas without easy access to supermarkets or grocery stores. Most of those people live in urban areas, where fast food and convenience shops replace healthy, nutritious foods as the most affordable option. Food insecurity is economic, but it also relates to community and health, with a higher risk of obesity, heart disease and cancer in areas with low access. In Michigan, organizations like the Detroit Black Community Food Sovereignty Network are advocating for urban farming and food sovereignty. items.t: At the oldest building in New Orleans, voices from the past come to life in new exhibit
items.x: NEW ORLEANS (WVUE) - Completed around 1752, the Old Ursuline Convent in the French Quarter is said to be the oldest surviving building in the Mississippi River valley. Now the Old Ursuline Convent Museum, there’s a new exhibit marking 300 years since the Ursuline nuns arrived in New Orleans. Sarah Waits, senior archivist at the Archdiocese of New Orleans, said back then, the sisters landed in a developing colony. “It was a wilderness. They talk about the mosquitoes and the alligators and just a huge cypress forest, and there were buffalo grazing along the river. It was a wild place,” said Sarah Waits. According to archdiocesan archives, 12 Ursuline nuns came to New Orleans in 1727 and eventually left the French Quarter in 1824. items.t: More than 42 million Americans have cast early midterm ballots
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - More than 42 million Americans have cast midterm ballots, and interesting demographic data shows who is voting. Michael McDonald, a University of Florida political scientist, said the U.S. could be headed toward record turnout. “It’s possible that we will beat the 2018 turnout rate. That was the highest turnout rate for midterm elections since 1914. But there are uneven patterns of turnout,” McDonald said. items.t: You’ll get an extra hour of sleep (or partying) on Halloween night as daylight saving time ends
items.x: (Gray News) — After a long night of trick-or-treating or partying, be prepared to get an extra hour of sleep. Daylight saving time will end on Nov. 1 at 2 a.m., also known as “fall back.” The United States will be back on standard time with more daylight in the morning and less in the evening. Daylight saving time will start again on March 14, 2027, also known as “spring forward.” The federal government has been discussing doing away with daylight saving time altogether, meaning clocks would not need to be changed at any point during the year. However, Congress failed to act before this weekend’s time change.

items.t: US Army practices digging mass battlefield graves
items.x: (Gray News) - The United States Army is now practicing mass battlefield graves, a practice not done since the Korean War. The Army reported that soldiers in North Carolina completed a “test-of-concept” exercise for large-scale battlefield temporary interment. “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management NCO for the 3rd CSC, in the release. Each plot is made up of five trenches designed to hold 100 bodies. During the exercises, soldiers reevaluated Korean War-era practices in how to excavate and backfill the plots without damaging the structure or human remains. The exercises also provided an opportunity for military chaplains and religious affairs specialists to train for mass-casualty environments.

items.t: Elizabethtown man charged after threat to blow up Bladen County courthouse
items.x: BLADEN COUNTY, N.C. (WECT) - A 44-year-old Elizabethtown man faces a felony charge after an email threatening to blow up the Bladen County courthouse prompted an investigation, authorities said. The Bladen County Sheriff’s Office said it received information about the email from the Bladen County District Attorney’s Office on Oct. 26. With help from the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation, investigators identified the email’s IP address. A subpoena led them to an address in the 300 block of Glenwood Drive in Elizabethtown. William Bryan Clark was charged with felony false bomb report. Clark was taken to the Bladen County Detention Center and initially held without bond. At his first appearance Oct. 30, a judge set his secured bond at $2 million.

items.t: The Beast of Bladenboro: A legend returns for Halloween weekend
items.x: BLADENBORO, N.C. (WECT) - In 1953, a mysterious animal terrorized Bladenboro and drew hunters to the small town. Today, the story lives on as a Halloween-weekend festival. “I was born two miles from here, and I was alive when the beast came through,” said Joyce Walters, who was a child at the time. She remembers it as a very fearful time. “A bloodthirsty creature came through and killed a lot of dogs, some goats, hogs. I understand it even killed a cow,” Walters said. People described the animal as a large, catlike creature — like a black panther, but with a furry tail, she said. Some believed it was a vampire beast because it crushed its prey’s skulls and drained their blood. “We didn’t have that many residents at that time, maybe 700 or 800 people but the population grew to 1,200 people or more because hunters came to hunt the beast,” Walters said.
